p0.original: 第十三章 表达感激

p4.original: “你这人真不错！昨晚开车送我回家。”
p4.en: "You're a good man! Drive me home last night.

p5.original: 赞扬也可能造成人与人之间的隔阂。这听起来似乎很奇怪。不过，请注意：在赞扬他人时，我们很少揭示内心活动，而把自己放在了裁判的位置。所以，我认为，赞扬并不总是有助于深化彼此的联系。
p5.en: A tribute may also create a gap between people. That sounds weird. However, note that, in praising others, we rarely reveal our inner activities and place ourselves in the hands of the referee. So, I believe that praise does not always help to deepen linkages.

p6.original: 在企业做培训时，常有经理人和我说，赞扬他人很管用。他们强调：“研究表明，如果经理赞扬员工，员工就会努力工作。在学校中，也存在同样的情况：如果老师表扬学生，学生就会认真学习。”虽然我也看过这类的研究报告，但我相信，这类的表扬无法持续地发挥作用。一旦意识到经理和老师赞扬的目的是为了操纵他们，员工和学生很可能就会产生逆反心理。然而，我最担心的是，发现这些赞扬的潜在目的之后，人们对于由衷的感激也会心存疑虑。
p6.en: In the course of training at the enterprise, managers often told me that praises were useful. They stressed: “The study shows that if managers praise their employees, they work hard. The same is true in schools: if a teacher praises a student, the student studies carefully. While I have also seen such studies, I am convinced that such praises will not work in a sustainable manner. Once it is realized that the purpose of the praises of managers and teachers is to manipulate them, it is likely that the staff and students will have a counter-spirited mind. However, I am most concerned that, once the potential purpose of these praises is found, there will also be doubts about the sincere gratitude.

p7.original: 此外，如果我们利用赞扬来施加影响，对方还可能误解我们的意思。
p7.en: Moreover, if we use praise to exert influence, the other side may also misconstrue our meaning.

p8.original: 有一幅卡通画讲了一个故事。
p8.en: There was a cartoon that told a story.

p9.original: 一位印第安人对另一位说：“看着，我现在用现代心理学来调教马！”接着，他领他的朋友走近他的马，大声地说道：“我的马是整个西部最快、最勇敢的马！”那匹马听后，十分悲伤，喃喃自语：“怎么办呢？我的主人抛弃了我，他买了另一匹整个西部最快、最勇敢的马！”
p9.en: One Indian said to another, "Look, I'm teaching horses with modern psychology! Then he led his friend to his horse, and he said, "My horse is the fastest and bravest horse in the whole west!" The horse heard it, and it was sad, and it said, "What do we do?" My master abandoned me. He bought another fastest and bravest horse in the whole West!

p10.original: 用非暴力沟通的方式表达感激时，我们只是为了庆祝他人的行为提升了我们的生活品质，而不是想得到任何回报。
p10.en: When we express our gratitude in a non-violent way, we only celebrate the behaviour of others that enhances the quality of our lives, not want any return.

p11.original: 非暴力沟通表达感激的方式
p11.en: A way to express gratitude for Nonviolent Communication

p12.original: 非暴力沟通表达感激的方式包含三个部分：
p12.en: The way Nonviolent Communication expresses gratitude consists of three parts:

p13.original: 1.对方做了什么事情使我们的生活得到了改善；
p13.en: 1. What the other party has done to improve our lives;

p14.original: 2.我们有哪些需要得到了满足；

p16.original: 在表达感激时，这三个部分的先后次序并不重要；有时，我们甚至可以通过微笑或说声“谢谢”来表达这三个部分。然而，如果我们要确保对方能够明白我们的意思，那么，用语言具体地描述这三个部分是值得的。以下是我和一个非暴力沟通研讨班参加者的一段对话。在对话中，我试图理解他为什么要赞扬我。
p16.en: In expressing gratitude, the order of the three components is not important; Sometimes we can even express these three parts by smiling or saying “thank you”. However, if we are to ensure that the other side understands what we mean, it is worthwhile to describe these three parts specifically in language. Here is a dialogue between me and a participant in a Nonviolent Communication workshop. In the course of the dialogue, I tried to understand why he would praise me.

p17.original: 参加者：（在研讨班结束后走近我）“马歇尔，你真了不起！”
p17.en: Participants: "Come to me after the seminar." Marshall, you're amazing!

p18.original: 马歇尔：“我想知道你为什么这么说。”
p18.en: "Marshall: I want to know why you said that.

p20.original: 马歇尔：“在我的一生中，人们用各种各样的话来评价我。这对我并没有多大的帮助。我需要更多的信息来理解你的评价。”
p20.en: Marshall: "In my life, people have judged me in a variety of words. It didn't help me that much. I need more information to understand your assessment.

p22.original: 马歇尔：“首先，我想知道，我做了什么，你认为对你的生活有帮助？”
p22.en: Marshall: “First, I want to know what I have done that you think will help your life?

p24.original: 马歇尔：“也许这又是一个评价。我还是不清楚我做了什么对你有益的事情。”
p24.en: Marshall: Maybe this is another evaluation. I still don't know what I did for you.

p25.original: 她想了想，然后拿出笔记本，指着其中的两段话说：“就是这两点。你今天在研讨班中提到它们。”
p25.en: She thought about it, and she took out the notebook, and she said, "That's it. You mentioned them today at the seminar.

p26.original: 马歇尔：“哦，你很欣赏这两个观点。”
p26.en: Marshall: "Oh, you appreciate these two ideas.

p28.original: 马歇尔：“听到这两个观点时，你的心情怎么样？”
p28.en: Marshall: "How do you feel when you hear these two ideas?

p29.original: 参加者：“我感觉一阵轻松，对将来更有信心了。”
p29.en: Participants: “I feel relieved and more confident about the future.

p30.original: 马歇尔：“现在，我想知道，这两个观点使你什么样的需要得到了满足？”
p30.en: Marshall: Now, I wonder what kind of needs have you met from these two perspectives?

p31.original: 参加者：“我没法和儿子沟通。他今年18岁了。我一直盼着能有办法和他沟通，你今天的这两个观点给我很大的启发。”
p31.en: Participants: “I can't communicate with my son. He's 18 years old. I've been looking forward to finding a way to communicate with him, and you've inspired me to these two points today.

p32.original: 这样，我就知道了我所做的事情、她的感受以及她的需要。我很高兴自己帮到了她。如果她一开始能够以非暴力沟通的方式表达感激，她也许就会说：“马歇尔，当你提到这两个观点时（让我看她的笔记本），我很欣喜，感到将来有盼头了，我一直在寻找和儿子沟通的办法，这两个观点给我很大的启发。”
p32.en: So I know what I'm doing, how she feels and what she needs. I'm glad I helped her. If she had been able to express her gratitude in a non-violent way at the outset, she might have said, “Marshall, when you mention these two points (let me look at her notebook), I am glad and I feel that there is hope for the future, and I have been looking for ways to communicate with my son, and these two points have been very enlightening to me.

p34.original: 在听到别人表达对我们的感激时，我们也许会觉得别扭。我们不知道自己是否真的那么好。我们甚至会担心别人对我们有所期待——特别是老师或经理试图通过赞扬来提高我们的学习和工作效率。此外，我们还可能担心在将来失去别人的赏识。
p34.en: We may find it awkward to hear others express our gratitude. We don't know if we're really that good. We would even fear that others expect us — particularly teachers or managers who try to improve our learning and productivity through praise. Moreover, we may fear losing others in the future.

p35.original: 生活在商品社会中，我们也许不太习惯单纯地付出与接受。然而，非暴力沟通鼓励我们注意倾听别人所表达的感激：我们做了什么有益的事情，他们有哪些需要得到了满足，以及这激发了他们怎样的情感。我们每个人都有能力提升他人的生活品质——这是一个值得铭记在心的事实。
p35.en: Living in a commodity society, we may be less accustomed to simply giving and accepting. However, Nonviolent Communication encourages us to listen to the gratitude expressed: what we have done usefully, what their needs have been met, and how it has inspired them. Each of us has the capacity to improve the quality of life of others — a fact worth remembering.

p36.original: 我从我的朋友纳菲滋·阿赛里（Nafez Assailey）那里学到了如何优雅地接受别人的感激。那时，无论是在巴勒斯坦，还是在以色列，举办有双方公民参加的研讨班，安全都是成问题的。于是，我请了一些巴勒斯坦人和以色列人来瑞士参加非暴力沟通研讨班。他是其中的一位巴勒斯坦人。在研讨班结束时，纳菲滋走到我面前说：“非暴力沟通对促进我们国家的和平非常有帮助，我们苏菲派穆斯林在表达特别的感激时有我们自己的方式，现在我想以这种方式来向你表示感谢。”他用大拇指扣住我的大拇指，看着我的眼睛，说道：“当我们生活在平静、爱与和谐之中，我们也就融为了一体。”接着，他吻了我的手。
p36.en: I learned from my friend Nafez Assailey how to receive the gratitude of others with grace. At that time, security was at stake, both in Palestine and in Israel, with seminars involving citizens from both sides. As a result, a number of Palestinians and Israelis were invited to Switzerland for a workshop on Nonviolent Communication. He is one of the Palestinians. At the end of the seminar, Nafiz came to me and said, “Nonviolent Communication is very helpful in promoting peace in our country, and we Sufi Muslims have our own way of expressing special gratitude, and I would like to thank you in that way. "He grabbed my thumb with his thumb and looked me in the eye and said, "When we live in peace, love and harmony, we are all one." Then he kissed my hand.

p37.original: 在别人表达感激时，人们通常有两种截然不同的反应。一种是自我膨胀，相信我们比别人优越；另一种是假谦虚，否定别人的欣赏，耸耸肩说：“哦，这没什么。” 纳菲滋帮助我看到了，我们有别的方式来听取感激。如果我意识到我的能力是生命赋予我的，我就能够同时避免自我膨胀和假谦虚。
p37.en: When others express gratitude, there are usually two distinct reactions. One is self-inflation, believing that we are superior to others; And the other one is false modesty, denial of appreciation, shrugging the shoulder and saying, "Oh, it's nothing. Nafis helped me see that we have another way to listen to gratitude. If I realize that my abilities are given to me by life, I will be able to avoid self-inflation and modesty at the same time.

p38.original: 以色列前总理哥达·梅厄（Golda Meir）曾经责备她的一位内阁部长：“不要那么谦虚，因为你没有那么伟大。”当代作家玛丽安·威廉森（Marianne Williamson）以下的一段话也提醒我不要假谦虚：
p38.en: The former Prime Minister of Israel, Golda Meir, blamed one of her cabinet ministers: “Don't be so modest, because you are not so great. “The current writer Marianne Williamson also reminds me not to be hypocritical:

p39.original: “我们最大的恐惧不是我们不够完美，
p39.en: “Our greatest fear is not that we are not perfect,

p40.original: 我们最大的恐惧是我们无比强大。
p40.en: Our greatest fear is our strength.

p41.original: 我们的光明，而不是我们的黑暗，让我们心存畏惧。你是上帝的孩子。你的小心翼翼帮不了这个世界。
p41.en: Our light, not our darkness, makes us afraid. You're the child of God. Your careless wings can't help the world.

p42.original: 缩小自己，好让周围的人在你身边不会觉得不自在，这并不明智。
p42.en: It would be unwise to shrink yourself so that people around you would not feel uncomfortable.

p43.original: 我们生下来就是为了彰显内在的荣光。那不仅存在于某些人，而是存在于每一个人！
p43.en: We were born to show our inner glory. It's not just in some people, it's in everyone!

p44.original: 当我们让自己的光芒闪耀，无意中我们也允许了他人散发光芒。
p44.en: When we shine our own light, we inadvertently allow others to shine.

p45.original: 一旦我们从自我的恐惧中解放出来，我们的存在，也会让他人得到解放。”
p45.en: Once we are freed from our fears, our presence will also free others.

p47.original: 虽然人们在听到感激时会不太自在，但绝大多数的人渴望得到他人的肯定和感激。在一次聚会中，为了让来宾互相认识，我的一位年仅12岁的朋友建议大家一起做一个游戏。我们每个人写下一个问题，放在一个盒子里，然后，轮流取出一个问题并大声作答。
p47.en: While people are not comfortable hearing gratitude, the vast majority of people are eager to receive recognition and gratitude from others. At a gathering, in order for guests to know each other, one of my friends, 12 years old, suggested that we all play a game together. Each of us writes the next question, puts it in a box, then turns out a question and answers it loudly.

p48.original: 在参加聚会前，我为一些社会工作者和公司职员提供了咨询服务，他们对感激的渴望深深触动了我。我常常听到这样的话：“不管你多努力工作，你都不会听到一句好话；但只要你犯了一点小错误，马上就会有人指责你。”于是，在聚会中，我写下了以下的问题：“别人对你做的什么事表达感激，你会欣喜若狂？”
p48.en: Prior to the meeting, I provided counselling services to social workers and company staff, whose desire for gratitude was deeply touched by me. I often hear the words: “No matter how hard you work, you will not hear a good word; But if you make a little mistake, you'll be blamed. So, at the party, I wrote the following question: “What else is there to thank you for what you did?

p49.original: 有位女士抽到了这个问题，读完之后，她哭了起来。这位女士负责管理一个妇女救助中心，这个机构为处于困境之中的妇女提供帮助。每个月，她都要精心制订工作计划，以使尽可能多的人得到帮助。然而，在每一次提出工作计划时，她都会听到一些抱怨。她投入这么多精力制定工作计划，但她想不起来，有任何人肯定过她的努力。一看到我的问题，她就想起了这件事，对感激的渴望让她流下了眼泪。
p49.en: A woman drew up the question, and she cried after reading. The woman runs a women's assistance centre, which provides assistance to women in difficult circumstances. Every month, she elaborates her programme of work so that as many people as possible can be helped. However, every time a programme of work was presented, she heard some complaints. She had devoted so much effort to developing a programme of work, but she could not remember that any one of her efforts had been confirmed. When she saw my problems, she remembered them, and her desire for gratitude sheds tears.

p50.original: 听了这位女士的故事之后，我的另一位朋友说他也想回答这个问题。接着，其他所有的人也表示愿意回答这个问题。在他们依次回答这个问题时，有几个人感动得哭了。
p50.en: Having heard the story of the woman, another friend of mine said that he also wanted to answer that question. Then all the others also expressed their willingness to answer the question. When they answered the question in turn, several people were moved to cry.

p51.original: 对感激的渴望不仅存在于工作场合，而且也存在于家庭中。有一天晚上，当我向我的儿子布莱特指出他没做好家务活时，他反驳说：“爸，你想想，你是不是倾向于指出问题，而很少肯定我？”他的话在我脑海中盘绕了许久。我发现我总是想做得更好，却很少肯定已有的成绩。我刚刚结束一个有100多人参加的研讨班，除了一个人，其他人都高度评价这次的研讨班。然而，我牢记的却是那个人的不满。
p51.en: The desire for gratitude exists not only in the workplace but also in the family. One night, when I pointed out to my son, Brett, that he wasn't doing his chores, he countered, "Daddy, do you think that you're inclined to point out the problem and rarely confirm me? His words have been in my mind for a long time. I find that I have always wanted to do better, but with little certainty of what has been achieved. I have just concluded a seminar with more than 100 participants, and all but one of them highly value it. However, what I remember is that person's dissatisfaction.

p52.original: 那天晚上，我意识到，在回顾个人经历时，我往往想到的是我做得不太好的2%，而不是做得不错的98%。我还想起了一位老师的教育方式。她的一位学生，因为没有做好考试准备，在一次考试中，写上名字交了白卷。当卷子发下来时，学生很惊讶，他发现他得了14分（满分100）。于是，他就去问老师：“我怎么会有14分呢？”她回答说：“整洁。”这次，布莱特又提醒了我，从那以后，我就更加留意生活中积极的一面，并表达我的感激之情。
p52.en: That night, I realized that in looking back at my personal experience, I often thought of 2 per cent of what I did not do well, rather than 98 per cent of what I did well. I also think of the way a teacher is educated. One of her students, who was not ready for the examination, wrote her name in a white paper at one of the examinations. When the rolls came out, the students were surprised and he found out that he had received 14 points (100 full points). So he went to the teacher, "How could I have 14 points?" And she said, "It's neat. This time, Brett reminded me that ever since then I have been more attentive to the positive aspects of life and expressed my gratitude.

p54.original: 约翰·鲍威尔（John Powell）在他的《爱的秘密》一书中讲到，对于没有在父亲活着的时候表达自己的感激，他十分伤心。这激起了我的强烈共鸣。如果无法向那些对我们的一生有极为重要影响的人表达感激，我们会感到多么悲哀啊！
p54.en: John Powell, in his book " The Secret of Love ", said that he was very sad not to express his gratitude when his father was alive. It aroused my strong resonance. How sad we would be if we could not express our gratitude to those who have had a very important impact on our lives.

p55.original: 当时，我立即想起了我的舅舅朱利叶斯·福克斯（Julius Fox）。在我小时候，他每日都来照顾我外祖母，那时，她已完全瘫痪。他在照顾我外祖母时，总是面带微笑，充满柔情。有些事情，在一个孩子看来，是很烦琐的；但对舅舅来说，照顾我外祖母仿佛是他求之不得的事情。舅舅向我展示了什么是真正的男子气——从那以后，舅舅的榜样就一直激励着我。
p55.en: At that time, I immediately remembered my uncle Julius Fox. When I was a child, he looked after my grandmother every day, when she was completely paralysed. He was always smiling and tender when he looked after my grandmother. Some things, in the eyes of a child, are cumbersome; But for my uncle, taking care of my grandmother seemed like something he couldn't help. My uncle showed me what real masculinity is - his role model has inspired me since then.

p56.original: 这时，我意识到了我还从未向舅舅表达过我的感激。当时，他病得很重，濒临死亡。我想和他说出心里话，却又有些犹豫。“我相信，他已经知道他对我有多重要；如果我说出来，也许他会感到尴尬。”当这个想法出现在我头脑中时，我就已经知道，它并不完全符合事实。我常常假定人们已经知道我的情意，然而，这是想当然。此外，即使人们在听到感激时会感到尴尬，他们也会想听到明确的表达。
p56.en: At that point, I realized I had never expressed my gratitude to my uncle. He was very ill and dying. I wanted to speak to him in my heart, but I hesitated. “I believe he knows how important he is to me; If I say so, maybe he'll be embarrassed. When that idea appeared in my mind, I knew that it was not entirely true. I often assume that I am already aware of my feelings, but of course I am. In addition, people would be embarrassed to hear gratitude, and they would like to hear it clearly.

p57.original: 想到这里，我还是有些犹豫，我担心语言无法表达出我心底深处的感受。我很快就克服了我的犹豫，虽然语言确实有其局限性，但我相信：“一件值得做的事情即使做得不怎么样也是值得的！”
p57.en: I'm still a little hesitant to think of it here, and I'm afraid that words are not able to express what I feel in my heart. I quickly overcome my hesitation, and while language does have its limitations, I believe: “A thing worth doing, if not doing it, is worth doing!”

p58.original: 在不久以后的一次家庭聚会中，我坐到了舅舅旁边，感激的话语从我心底涌了出来。舅舅很开心，没有丝毫尴尬。那天晚上，我很激动，回家后还写了首诗寄给他。舅舅在三周后去世了。我后来得知，舅舅每天都请人读那首诗给他听。
p58.en: I sat next to my uncle at a family meeting shortly after, and the words of gratitude came out of my heart. Uncle's happy, not at all embarrassed. That night, I was so excited that I went home and wrote him a poem. His uncle died three weeks later. I was told that my uncle invited him to read the poem every day.

p60.original: 在赞扬他人时，我们很少揭示内心活动，而把自己放在了裁判的位置。赞扬也常常被人用来实现个人目的。非暴力沟通鼓励我们充分表达感激。在表达感激时，我们说出：（1）对我们有益的行为；（2）我们的哪些需要得到了满足；（3）我们的需要得到满足后，我们是什么样的心情。
p60.en: In praising others, we rarely reveal our inner activities and place ourselves in the hands of the referee. Commendation is also often used for personal purposes. Nonviolent Communication encourages us to express our full gratitude. In expressing our gratitude, we say: (i) Acts that are good for us; (2) Which of our needs have been met; (3) What do we feel when our needs are met?

p61.original: 当别人以这样的方式表达对我们的感激时，我们可以与对方一起庆祝生命的美——既不自大，也不假谦虚。
p61.en: When others express their gratitude to us in such a way, we can celebrate the beauty of life with each other — neither arrogance nor modesty.
